title: Flaming Cliffs (Bayn Dzak), Djadokhta Formation, Mongolia
summary: At Bayn Dzak, the Flaming Cliffs of Mongolia’s Gobi, the Djadokhta Formation records a Cretaceous dunefield with shallow interdune ponds. American Museum expeditions in 1922–25 found dinosaur eggs and nests, complete Protoceratops skeletons, Cretaceous mammals and theropods including Velociraptor, Saurornithoides and Oviraptor. Magnetic dating suggests, without proving, a late Campanian age of about 75 to 71 million years.

uncertainty.note: Dashzeveg et al. (2005) suggest but do not firmly establish 75 to 71 Ma; earlier faunal ages ranged from Cenomanian to earliest Maastrichtian. The Natural History Museum gives 74 to 70 Ma for Velociraptor in the Gobi.

as_recorded.value: late part of the Campanian between about 75 to 71 Ma

beats.caption: Cross-bedded dune sands with shallow interdune ponds built the Bayn Dzak Member of the Djadokhta Formation, probably in late Campanian time.
The American Museum’s Central Asiatic Expedition worked here in 1922–23 and 1925, finding dinosaur eggs and nests and complete Protoceratops skeletons.
In 1971 a Velociraptor and Protoceratops preserved together were found at Tugrugyin Shireh, about 50 km northwest, in the same formation.
